model_result.answer_summary: Structures for the AFM synthesis of cyclo[14]carbon (question 6.2). From printed arrow stoichiometry on Q6-1 (C14Cl10; A -2Cl·, B -5Cl· from A, C -2Cl· from B, D -3Cl· from A, -1Cl· to C14): B = C14Cl3, intact anthracene skeleton, chlorine remaining on {lt, lbl, rl}, two unpaired electrons retained on the meso carbons cu· and cl· (the 9,10-dehydroanthracene diradical). C = C14Cl1, single chlorine on lt, central ring opened by the retro-Bergman mechanism drawn in scheme (1): exactly bonds jb-cl and cl-jrB broken (the 1,4-diradical junction pair carrying the alkyne arm), the two unpaired electrons now on junctions jb· and jrB·. D = C14Cl5 (from A, -3Cl·), intact skeleton, chlorine on {lt, ltu, lb, lbl, rl}, three unpaired electrons (meso cu·, cl· plus rt·). Verified: 10-2-5-2-1 = 0, A->D 8->5.
assumptions: Anthracene skeleton: 14 carbons, 16 sigma bonds, three linearly fused six-membered rings (jt jb jrT jrB = junctions; cu, cl = meso carbons)
Peripheral (degree-2) carbons {cu, cl, lt, ltu, lb, lbl, rt, rr, rb, rl} carry exactly one substituent (Cl or H); junctions never carry Cl (as drawn on the sheet)
Each AFM Cl· abstraction removes exactly one chlorine and leaves one unpaired electron on the abstraction site (the note in 6.2)
Retro-Bergman step is the ring opening shown in scheme (1): two central-ring sigma bonds adjacent to the 1,4-diradical junction pair are broken, converting the opened path to an alkyne arm

Positional choices among symmetry-inequivalent peripheral chlorines where the AFM images are not decisive: B keeps Cl on {lt, lbl, rl}; D's third radical is on rt (minimal-changes reading of the printed A drawing)
source_gaps: The grey-scale AFM frames do not uniquely identify which of the (symmetry-equivalent under the page's own drawing) peripheral chlorines survive in B or which arc is dechlorinated in D; only formulas, radical counts, intact-vs-opened state, and the identity of the opened bond pair are forced by the problem data alone. All forced data are fixed and proved.
